text: By the Upward Lowenheim-Skolem theorem, if a theory $T$ has an infinite model of cardinality $\kappa$, then:
choices: $T$ has a model of every cardinality $\lambda \geq \kappa$
$T$ has a unique model up to isomorphism
explanation: Upward Lowenheim-Skolem yields models of every cardinality $\lambda \geq \kappa$. This is exactly why no first-order theory can pin an infinite structure down to a unique model up to isomorphism (ruling out the last option). It produces LARGER models, not only countable ones (that is the downward version), and says nothing about completeness.
